title: ArbiterQ: Improving QNN Convergency and Accuracy by Applying Personalized Model on Heterogeneous Quantum Devices
problem: In the NISQ era, training and inference on heterogeneous quantum devices is hindered by limited qubits, device noise, and frequent online/offline transitions. Naive distributed QNN approaches destroy accuracy due to device heterogeneity and instability.
motivation: Leveraging multiple quantum devices can increase computational capacity, but heterogeneity and noise make coordination difficult; personalized models per device are needed.
method: ArbiterQ customizes a quantum neural network (machine-learning model on quantum hardware) for each quantum processor by building two profiles: model vector (the mathematical parameters the network learns) and behavioral vector (measurements of how that specific processor performs). During training, it shares gradient updates (improvements to the model) between processors with similar behavioral profiles, allowing them to work in parallel while accounting for hardware differences. It also optimizes inference—running the trained model—by scheduling tasks (shot-oriented inference scheduling) to balance workload and improve accuracy.
key_novelty: The core innovation is personalizing quantum neural networks to each processor's behavioral profile (measurements of its actual hardware performance), then sharing training improvements between processors with similar profiles to enable distributed training across heterogeneous quantum hardware.
contributions: Model vector and behavioral vector dual representation for device-aware personalization
Gradient sharing among similar-behavior QPUs for efficient parallelism
Shot-oriented inference scheduling for fine-grained workload balancing
4.03x training speedup with 7.87% loss reduction vs. EQC
primary_theme: Personalized QNN models for heterogeneous quantum devices
